claims.sentence: In 2025 and 2026, references to works that do not exist were found in papers accepted at NeurIPS \citep{ansari2026compound,russinovich2026phantom}, ACL identified more than 100 accepted papers citing non-existent literature during camera-ready checks \citep{acl2026statement}, and ICLR and ICML now treat such references as grounds for desk rejection \citep{iclr2026response,russinovich2026phantom}.
claims.claim: ICLR treats hallucinated (non-existent) references as grounds for desk rejection (the ICML part is attributed to russinovich2026phantom).
claims.excerpt: Extensive and/or careless LLM usage often results in false claims, misrepresentations, or hallucinated content, including hallucinated references. As stated in our previous blog post: hallucinations of this kind would be considered a Code of Ethics violation on the part of the paper's authors. We have been desk -rejecting, and will continue to desk -reject, any paper that includes such issues.
claims.note: Minor: the post states the ICLR 2026 policy (Nov 2025); 'now' is supported for the 2026 cycle only. Action is taken only when an AC or SAC finds concrete evidence.
